text:
First off you run the cleanest,  most informative and most well-thought out channel of this time by such a wide margin that it almost feels like meditating compared to some of the other bitter clowns in this arena. On that note I feel like there is so much widespread animosity toward the 3070 ti specifically in the tech review community from nothing more than review fatigue, both in terms of the sheer number of cards coming your way and the fact that crypto fluctuations could make you eat your (collective as a community) words at any moment. I'm also noticing that almost all of the critique universally involves benchmarks as a reference point to 3070 and 3080 numbers. Everyone pissed about the tiny percentage gains over the 3070 and the gap with the 3080, but tech reviewers are literally the ONLY people on the planet with 5 of these cards sitting in one room with a configuration that even allows this type of comparison to take place. I think you are the only one to constantly mention the caveat that it will ultimately come down to whatever card is in the  sweet spot cost-wise at the time of buying. I just don't get the point of seething about incremental gains between models where the 3070 ti was shoved after the other two debuted. I am in a strangely unique position having bought a Radeon VII on eBay a few years back for about $850, which I just sold for $1600 on eBay yesterday (which is on the low-end for those cards still). I tried for hours to find a 3080 or 6800XT that came close to the $1050 the 3070ti founders edition was sitting at. Not everyone has my level of dumb luck to be able to cash out on a card (Radeon VII) actually deserving of most of the ridicule it received, but even in my case I was facing some out of pocket costs to step up into what you call the premium range or getting the 3070ti and having enough leftover to pair it with a 2TB Gen 4 nvme and effectively eliminate the two bottles that still existing in my 3960X rig that I built. I didn't do my normal amount of research before pulling the trigger on the 3070ti because you never know what tomorrow will bring, so it's only after committing the money that I came to all the vitriol aimed at my new baby. I freaked at first until I realized it was all a bunch of reviewers who were (justifiably) grumpy that they had to review another nVidia card that occupies a questionable space in the entire 3000 product line up when all your audience can reply back is that they can't ge their hands on any of them.

Though we are borderline psychotic when researching a purchase, unless you totally whiffed or made a blind buy right before a new product launch, as long as it feels noticeably faster than what you had before at the things you need it for the most, all of this indignant bluster seems like crying over a glass of milk that only one person can drink and most people don't even know existed because no one feels those feels and thinks "dammit I am only 7% happier than I would have been with a 3070." I honestly find it a disservice to the legions of people who come to this community for the holiest of advice about which beating heart to put in the most important machine  in your life that can't fit in a pocket. Thank you for keeping it heady and always seeming to enjoy what you are doing because you're helping the rest of us make sense of this crazy past year while all the others have a pity party and call it a review.

text:
@nathancheema1091  I have so many doubts about buying a GPU. If you can help me clear it please do that would be wonderful.
Does the manufacturer in the GPU matter ( MSI, GIGABYTE, ASUS, GALAX ) which one do I go for ?
I want to buy a GPU for gaming purposes only so do i choose a GPU with LHR or Non LHR ?
Do I buy a 3070ti or 3080 ? 
What are the differences in the editions i.e. Founders Edition, gaming trio , suprim x ? 
I am planning to build a pc in Jan 2022 will the price of GPU come down at that time ?
author: @L.Abhinav

text: @L.Abhinav  I'm not an expert but I can give you a rough idea. Brands don't matter much but obviously certain brands have better goodwill then others or have better reliability. Best off looking into that if it concerns you. Best to look at each gpu individually and see their thermals, power draw and size of the card itself. As for which gpu you are Best getting it depends on what you want out of it. 1080p or 1440p you will be more cpu bound so a 3060 or 3070 will do great but 4k gaming if your looking at reliable 60 you are going to need a 3080 minimum. LHR for what I have seen doesn't effect gaming so ignore that unless you plan on mining at some point.
author: @nathancheema1091

text: @L.Abhinav  with the shortages honestly it is hard to tell if gpu prices will fall soon if you want my opinion I don't see prices falling till at least late 2022 possible even 2023. Here's hoping it does though cause the 3000 series gpus are awesome and it is definately worth a buy.
author: @nathancheema1091

text: @nathancheema1091  so do I buy one which doesn't have LHR on it then ?
author: @L.Abhinav

text: @L.Abhinav  a non LHR card will game the same as a LHR one. LHR cards just have a higher hash rate which helps with gpu mining. They introduced the non LHR cards so miners wouldn't be interested in them and the gpus would actually make it to gamers...well least that was the plan anyway.

text:
You are completely and utterly wrong. I've seen a lot of advice in the current market, but this is probably the worst. 

Regarding the Ryzen 50xx chip. You can run basically anything decently on this chip. Also note that these are integrated graphics. This is extremely cheap if you consider that you are getting an CPU in that price as well. Yes, it isn't going to give you 30xx performance, or even close, but that is also saving you $1000-$3000 so I'd say it is more then a good idea if you want to upgrade it later when the market is better. It is not meant to be a dedicated graphics card yet can run modern games decently as a backup. If you have a 1080 I'd recommend holding onto it, but anything older and need an upgrade because your PC is simply old? The best thing you can get if you are into gaming.

Also, what kind of advice is "maybe get a console" in a video about best and worst GPUs? Don't people realize that you need to own console games for that? What I am supposed to do with my 150 PC games on a PS5?  Horrible advice. You get a console for the games or if you are new to gaming, and even then it is really not a choice for those who have a budget in mind long term.  Don't get me wrong there is a place for consoles, but that is such bad advice given the context of the video.

Here is a great comparison of multiple games 5600G: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCbybCYLJog

I'd say the graph for price comparison was interesting though, respect for the research, even if the prices are completely different per country, from week to week, let alone per region. text: Excellent video, but not without flaw. You failed to mention VRAM, power consumption, overclocking, software, or driver overhead.. Now most people don't overclock their GPUs, and I can understand why, but it is free performance. Just a little tinkering around and you have you have yourself ~10% performance boost at no additional cost. AMD allows you overclock your GPU within the Adrenaline Software, and 'stress test' your settings too. I recently bought and used a Nvidia based gaming laptop, and I was reminded of how archaic Nvidia's control panel really is, its just a list of settings you scroll through. It looks like a game menu from 2002. GeForce Now also kinda blows. Now at least it looks modern, but the 'optimized' settings guides for games are completely useless. Not to mention the driver overhead issue with low end CPUs, or decent CPUs in CPU heavy titles. Take Battlefield V for example, you are going to be CPU bottlenecked even at 4K @ Max settings on a 3080 and beyond. I bet that part of the reason why Nvidia GPUs lag behind AMD GPUs in BFV is because of the driver overhead. When pushing a ton of frames in BFV the CPU takes a beating, and any additional load placed on it could affect performance. Hardware Unboxed has made several videos on the topic, I would have thought that you would have seen them. Now VRAM is another problem that hurts Nvidia's lineup, there are games out now that can utilize more that 10 GB of VRAM, Red Dead Redemption 2 is a prime example. I have seen usage peak at 15.8 GB in that game on my 6900 XT. Red Dead Redemption is a 2019 title, which is Nvidia sponsored to boot, and Nvidia's 'flagship' barely scrapes by. The 3080, 3070 Ti, and the 3070 are high end GPUs, meant for 1440p + gaming, except they have 10 GB and 8 GB of VRAM respectively. No one should be recommending a 3070 or 3070 Ti over a 6700 XT or a 6800.

text:
If you're desperate for a graphics card, you probably want to look to the used market. However, I think the most important thing is probably to simply go with one of the cheapest cards which will allow you to play some of the games you like at decent settings. I would recommend considering an AMD APU, GT 1030 (but only if it has DDR5 memory), or GTX 1050 ti, or something else of a similar price and performance level (like maybe a higher or mid-range level card from a really old generation like GTX 600 or HD 7000 series). Or you could go with something even weaker than that maybe. 

Maybe think of it this way: Now is a great time to start looking up classic older games, or just very simple newer Indy games with very low system requirements.

Older gamers like myself will almost universally agree that many of the classic games from more than 10 or even 20+ years ago still hold up today as better games than most of the contemporary games you see for sale today. Not all games rely on a modern level of graphical fidelity to be very enjoyable, rewarding, or even to be immersive and/or beautiful (in rarer cases). 

We all need to show card makers that we are not so desperate for new videocards that we will be willing to pay such grossly inflated prices. It's simply not right to allow them to make so much of a higher profit margin per unit. Prices will come back down if they're not making enough sales. If there was a total monopoly, then they might be able to get away with selling at these prices indefinitely, but there are at least four fabs and at least three GPU designer companies which are all capable of fabricating/ designing graphics cards which would be very price competitive in the current market. I still am not totally sure why AMD hasn't seemed to have shown much of an interest in making GPUs using GloFlo. Is it just that they keep underestimating just how strong demand for current gen graphics cards is going to continue to be, and how long it will last, and so haven't wanted to take the risk of investing in production which likely would take a really long time to set up again?

Going down below 4k instantly hit AMD the win, especially turning on Smart access memory (for this AM4 board (like x570) and a ryzen chip lets say 5800x) will be needed to unlock this potential. At this point AMD will win any game.

So: 3080/6800XT
4k and Ray: Nvidea, GDDR6X (1.5x the speed of GDDR6 memory)
Below 4k , SAM (smart access memory) and the infinity cache which i didnt name (2.17x bit bus speeds in the same bus size) (256x2.17=555.52bit buss speeds)

In essence, They are more or like the same. Turning off raytracing and going below 4k native (upscaling will give AMD the win to 4k) will give AMD the win. but both just barely in front of another

text:
A LOT of OTHER youtubers keep saying the lack of GPU's is due to components. I can tell you right now, that is absolute bullshit. Because those parts they speak of, I can right now purchase them no issue. If they were really hard to get, then it would be hard to get for consumers like myself too. These businesses do not have problems with these extra parts.

THE REAL ISSUE, at least on AMD's end, was the FACT that consoles were eating 80% of their 7nm capacity at TSMC. This news dropped middle of 2020 from taiwan news sources (yes, having to use google translate). When 80% of your fabrication is being allocated to two xbox chips and one ps5 chip, you end up with only 20% left for cpu and gpu. And guess what, that is most likely 15% cpu and 5% cpu, or a worse 19% cpu and 1% gpu.... Either way, it explains the low gpu stock.

Now some people might then argue, what about Nvidia? They were making their gpu's over at samsung, and they don't make consoles. So they aren't limited like AMD. Well, the answer there is Nvidia's greed. YES, they could sell one gpu at a time to gamers at fair prices, undercutting AMD. But knowing that AMD had card limitations, they decided to sell cards directly to miners. This means they net a higher profit as they can jack the prices slightly higher. They also skip the middle man aka companies like EVGA and ASUS and instead are selling "directly" to miners. Which means more profit.

Those two things explain EVERYTHING. This idea that there are shortage of "power components" or whatever most youtubers are claiming, is a bullshit lie. Only a handful of companies actually have issues with supply, and its their own fault because the parts they lack, are parts they make! An example would be OLED. There is a company who makes MICRO-OLED (really tiny, like 1" screens) who claimed they had a shortage of components, but they MAKE those components. So their own shortcomings was because of their own lack of production. If you read just the title to those news articles, you would think EVERYONE has issues with supply. Except you can't just read headlines, they are always misleading "click bait" forcing you to read the contents to get the real picture. So in reality, the lack of gpu's right now is a mix between consoles taking up production capacity for AMD and Nvidia selling directly to miners.

I really wish Ali was a bit more realistic with the US GPU pricing. I think people would kill for 3080 pricing that was sub $1k. That's simply not the case right now. Either you find the very very rare eVGA FTW at $890...or you're left with ridiculous MSI / Asus pricing that goes from $1,100 to $1,200. Likewise his price of 3080Ti being below $1,400 is not realistic at all. Only the eVGA model goes for $1,399 - and it's very hard to find, which leaves the Gigabyte model at $1,480 and then everyone else (MSI/Asus) who start at $1,700 and go as high as $2,000. Yes, $2,000 for a 3080Ti. IMO, box/whisker graphs would've been the better listing and I worry that people will get overly optimistic looking at the numbers he has posted here. 

I think buying GPUs right now is a matter of expectations. Builders should go in expecting to only see the overpriced MSI/Asus cards, but in the rare chance that eVGA stock is available, then there is some pricing relief. Anyway, my tl;dr is that's it's still worse than Ali is presenting.
